description: Dunit Userspace ABI v0 conformance — the roadmap's M6.3 'done' gate: an independent freestanding C program (no musl), built with the host C compiler against the generated ABI headers (abi/include/dunit) and the Dunit crt0 (userspace/ctests/crt0.s), reads its arguments/environment off the SysV initial stack, makes raw syscalls, respects the errno contract, and exits correctly. The program /app/c_hello is launched from the terminal; its stdout is mirrored to serial. Proves the C side of the ABI works end to end before any libc port. Run: tools/qemu_test.py --build --markers-file tools/m6_c_abi_markers.json --post-boot-delay 3 --settle 3 --timeout 110 --boot-timeout 80

required.claim: the system booted to the terminal
the freestanding C program's crt0 reached main() via the Dunit process-entry ABI
C read argc/argv off the SysV initial stack (not registers) — argv[0] is the program name
argv is NULL-terminated, envp present, and a bad-fd write returned -EBADF (errno contract reaches C) — full ABI v0 conformance

forbidden.why: the C ABI conformance program failed a check
